items.label: section_header
items.text: WHATISABUFFERSOLUTION?

items.label: text
items.text: Many experiments,particularly in biochemistry,have to be performedinaqueoussolutionsoffairlyconstantpH.Unfortunately, itisimpossibletomakeasolutionwhosepHistotallyunaffected by the addition ofevensmall amountsofacid orbase.However, it is possible to make a solution whose pH remains almost unchanged whensmall amountsofacidorbaseareadded.Such asolution is called abuffersolution.

items.label: text
items.text: There are many ways of making a buffer solution, but two of the mostcommonare:

items.label: list_item
items.text: ·to mix a weak acid with its conjugate base

items.label: list_item
items.text: .to mix a weak base with its conjugate acid.

items.label: section_header
items.text: BUFFERMADEFROMAWEAKACIDANDITSCONJUGATEBASE

items.label: text
items.text: Thesimplestexampleof thisis ethanoicacid and sodiumethanoate.Thesaltoftheweakacidhastobesolublein used tomakebuffersolutions.

items.label: text
items.text: In this mixture the acid is partially dissociated, whereas the salt is fully dissociated. The relevant equations are:

items.label: text
items.text: CH;COOH(aq) = CH;COO-(aq) + H+(aq)

items.label: text
items.text: CH;COONa(aq) → CH;COO-(aq) + Na+(aq)

items.label: text
items.text: This mixturewill produce a buffer solution with a pH less than7. TheexactpHdependsontheconcentrationofbothacid andits conjugate base, and can be calculated as follows.

items.label: section_header
items.text: CALCULATINGTHEpHOFABUFFERSOLUTION

items.label: text
items.text: For our examplewe will use a solution that has been made by mixing equal volumes of 1.00 mol dm-3ethanoic acid and 1.00moldm-3sodiumethanoateat298K.

items.label: text
items.text: Ifweassumethattheextentofdissociationoftheacidis negligible,then the concentration of CHCOOH at equilibrium will be 0.500 moldm-3.

items.label: text
items.text: Also,againbecause thedissociationofthe acid isnegligible,the concentrationoftheethanoateionsatequilibriumcanbe considered tobe entirely madeupfrom thesodiumsalt.So,theconcentration of ethanoate ions at equilibrium is also 0.500 mol dm-3.

items.label: text
items.text: Notethattheconcentrationofbothacid andsaltinthemixtureis halfoftheconcentrationsusedbecauseequalvolumesofeach solutionweremixed.Thetotalvolumeofthemixtureistwicethat of theoriginalvolume ofeach solutionused.

items.label: text
items.text: At 298K,

items.label: formula
items.text: Ka = [CH₃COO⁻(aq)][H⁺(aq)] / [CH₃COOH(aq)] = 1.74 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³

items.label: text
items.text: Rearranging this equation and substituting values for [CH;COOH(aq)] and [CH;COO-(aq)] gives:

items.label: text
items.text: This gives a pH for the buffer solution of 4.76.

items.label: section_header
items.text: LEARNINGTIP

items.label: text
items.text: Apotential trapwhencalculatingthepHofabuffersolutionisnot understandingthatwhentwosolutionsaremixedthereisadilution. If50cmofonesolutionismixedwith50cm3ofanothersolution, thenthetotalvolumeofthemixturewillbe100cm3.So,the concentration of each solution will be halved onmixing.

items.label: section_header
items.text: HOWDOESTHEBUFFERACTIONWORK?

items.label: text
items.text: Whenasmallamountofacidisaddedtothebuffersolution,the majority of the H+ions added react with the CHCOO-ions to form CHCOOH molecules:

items.label: text
items.text: CH;COO-(aq) + H+(aq) → CH;COOH(aq)

items.label: text
items.text: When a little base is added,the majority of the OH-ions added reactwiththeCHCOOHmolecules:

items.label: text
items.text: CH;COOH(aq) + OH-(aq) → CH;COO-(aq) + H2O(l)

items.label: text
items.text: Anewequilibriummixturewill beestablishedinwhichthe concentrationsofbothCHCOOH and CHCOO-willhavechanged slightly from their original values. So, there willbe a change in pH, but this willbe minimal. This is shown by the following argument.

items.label: text
items.text: To show that the pH has changed very little,we once again need tomake use of the expressionforKaofthe acid:

items.label: formula
items.text: Ka = [CH₃COO⁻(aq)][H⁺(aq)] / [CH₃COOH(aq)]

items.label: text
items.text: Rearranging this equation gives:

items.label: formula
items.text: [H⁺(aq)] = Ka × [CH₃COOH(aq)] / [CH₃COO⁻(aq)]

items.label: text
items.text: As there are a relatively large number of CHCOOH molecules in thesolution,astheextentofdissociationoftheacidisverysmall, the change in [CH;COOH(aq)] will be negligible.
